name: Learn: Scheduling
description: Master how pods land on nodes — node labels + nodeSelector, taints & tolerations, nodeAffinity, manual scheduling with nodeName, and running one pod per node with a DaemonSet.
objective: CKA › Workloads & Scheduling (15%). Goal: control where pods land — labels/nodeSelector, taints & tolerations, nodeAffinity, manual scheduling, and DaemonSets.

questions.title: Labels + nodeSelector
questions.teach:
A pod's `spec.nodeSelector` is the simplest way to steer scheduling: the pod only lands on a node whose labels contain **every** key/value listed (exact equality, AND'ed). Label a node with `kubectl label node <node> key=value`, then put the same key/value under `spec.nodeSelector`.

**Gotcha:** if no node matches the selector, the pod stays `Pending` forever — check `kubectl describe pod` events.
questions.prompt:
A worker node named like `$W1` exists. Label it `disktype=ssd`, then in namespace `sched-learn` create a pod `ssd-pod` (image `busybox:1.36`, command `sleep 3600`) with a `nodeSelector` of `disktype=ssd`.

Target: pod `ssd-pod` is `Running` and its `.spec.nodeName` equals the labeled node.
questions.hint: `kubectl label node "$W1" disktype=ssd`, then build the pod YAML with `spec.nodeSelector.disktype: ssd` (or `kubectl run ssd-pod --image=busybox:1.36 --overrides=... -- sleep 3600`).
questions.solution:
kubectl label node "$W1" disktype=ssd --overwrite
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: ssd-pod
  namespace: sched-learn
spec:
  nodeSelector:
    disktype: ssd
  containers:
  - name: c
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
EOF

verification.description: ssd-pod is Running on the node labeled disktype=ssd

questions.title: Taints + tolerations
questions.teach:
A **taint** repels pods that don't tolerate it — `kubectl taint node <node> key=value:NoSchedule`. A pod opts in with a matching **toleration** (`key`, `value`, `effect`) under `spec.tolerations`.

**Gotcha:** a toleration only *permits* scheduling onto the tainted node, it doesn't *attract* the pod there — pair it with a `nodeSelector`/affinity (as this task does) to actually land on that node.
questions.prompt:
Taint node `$W1` with `workload=batch:NoSchedule`. Then in `sched-learn` create pod `batch-pod` (`busybox:1.36`, `sleep 3600`) that **tolerates** that taint AND uses a `nodeSelector`/affinity so it lands on `$W1`.

Target: `batch-pod` is `Running` on `$W1` (proving the toleration let it through the taint).
questions.hint: `kubectl taint node "$W1" workload=batch:NoSchedule`. Give the pod a toleration `{key: workload, value: batch, effect: NoSchedule}` plus `nodeSelector: {disktype: ssd}` (reuse step 1's label) so it targets $W1.
questions.solution:
kubectl taint node "$W1" workload=batch:NoSchedule --overwrite
kubectl label node "$W1" disktype=ssd --overwrite
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: batch-pod
  namespace: sched-learn
spec:
  nodeSelector:
    disktype: ssd
  tolerations:
  - key: workload
    operator: Equal
    value: batch
    effect: NoSchedule
  containers:
  - name: c
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
EOF

verification.description: node $W1 is tainted and batch-pod tolerates it and runs there

questions.title: nodeAffinity (requiredDuringScheduling)
questions.teach:
**nodeAffinity** (under `spec.affinity.nodeAffinity`) is a richer nodeSelector using `matchExpressions` with operators like `In`, `NotIn`, `Exists`, `Gt`, `Lt`. The **hard** form `requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` must be satisfied or the pod stays `Pending`.

**Gotcha:** affinity attracts but doesn't defeat taints — a tainted target node still needs a toleration, hence this pod's `tolerations: [{operator: Exists}]`.
questions.prompt:
Node `$W1` is labeled `tier=gold`. In `sched-learn` create pod `affinity-pod` (`busybox:1.36`, `sleep 3600`) using **required** nodeAffinity matching `tier In [gold]`.

Target: `affinity-pod` is `Running` on the node labeled `tier=gold`.
questions.solution:
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: affinity-pod
  namespace: sched-learn
spec:
  affinity:
    nodeAffinity:
      requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
        nodeSelectorTerms:
        - matchExpressions:
          - key: tier
            operator: In
            values: ["gold"]
  tolerations:
  - operator: Exists
  containers:
  - name: c
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
EOF

verification.description: affinity-pod is Running on the node labeled tier=gold

questions.title: Manual scheduling with nodeName
questions.teach:
Setting `spec.nodeName` directly **bypasses the scheduler** — the kubelet on that exact node just picks the pod up and runs it. Use it to pin a pod deterministically or when the scheduler is unavailable.

**Gotcha:** a wrong/nonexistent node name does **not** error — the pod sits `Pending` with no scheduler event, since no scheduler ever looked at it. Copy the exact name from `kubectl get nodes`.
questions.prompt:
In `sched-learn` create pod `manual-pod` (`busybox:1.36`, `sleep 3600`) that is bound to worker node `$W2` **via `spec.nodeName`** (no nodeSelector/affinity).

Target: `manual-pod` is `Running` and `.spec.nodeName` == `$W2`.
questions.hint: Add `nodeName: <the $W2 node name>` at the top of `spec`. Find the name with `kubectl get nodes`.
questions.solution:
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: manual-pod
  namespace: sched-learn
spec:
  nodeName: $W2
  containers:
  - name: c
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
EOF

verification.description: manual-pod is Running and pinned to $W2 via nodeName

questions.title: DaemonSet (one pod per node)
questions.teach:
A **DaemonSet** runs one copy of a pod on every matching node, adding/removing pods as nodes join/leave. Like a Deployment but with no `replicas`, and `spec.selector.matchLabels` must match the pod template labels.

**Gotcha:** control-plane nodes carry a `NoSchedule` taint, so to cover *every* node the pod template needs a broad toleration — `tolerations: [{operator: Exists}]` tolerates all taints.
questions.prompt:
In `sched-learn` create a DaemonSet `node-agent` (`busybox:1.36`, `sleep 3600`, label `app=node-agent`) with a toleration broad enough (`operator: Exists`) to run on **every** node including the control plane.

Target: the DaemonSet has one ready pod on each node — `desiredNumberScheduled` == number of nodes and `numberReady` matches.
questions.hint: DaemonSet selector `app=node-agent`, pod template tolerations `- operator: Exists`. Verify with `kubectl -n sched-learn get ds node-agent` and `kubectl get nodes`.
questions.solution:
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: node-agent
  namespace: sched-learn
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: node-agent
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: node-agent
    spec:
      tolerations:
      - operator: Exists
      containers:
      - name: c
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["sleep","3600"]
EOF

verification.description: DaemonSet node-agent runs one ready pod on every node
